reference_sql:
SELECT p.brand, COUNT(*) AS n_checks
FROM competitor_prices cp
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = cp.product_id
WHERE cp.observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03 00:00:00' AND cp.observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-10 00:00:00'
GROUP BY p.brand
alternatives: SELECT p.brand, COUNT(*) AS n_checks FROM products p JOIN competitor_prices cp ON cp.product_id = p.product_id WHERE CAST(cp.observed_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-03-03' AND DATE '2025-03-09' GROUP BY p.brand
SELECT p.brand, COUNT(*) AS n_checks FROM competitor_prices cp JOIN products p ON p.product_id = cp.product_id WHERE date_trunc('week', cp.observed_ts) = TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1

other_way.sql: SELECT p.brand, COUNT(*) AS n_checks FROM competitor_prices cp JOIN products p ON p.product_id = cp.product_id WHERE date_trunc('week', cp.observed_ts) = TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1
other_way.tradeoff: Truncating to the Monday of each week matches here, but only because the range is exactly one whole ISO week.
